title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 138
paragraphs: The king's expedition was called, in name, an expedition against Athens; but in fact it was aimed at all of Greece. The Greeks, long since informed of it, were not all affected in the same way. Some of them, having given earth and water to the Persian, were confident, expecting that they would suffer no injury from the barbarian; while others, who had not given, were in great fear, seeing that there were not ships enough in Greece to receive the invader in battle as far as numbers went, and that the majority of the states were unwilling to take up the war but readily embraced the side of the Medes.
